decisions.reason: Freedom to choose a source YouTube video does not change the required short-form publication channels.
The source-video choice does not alter the requirement that selected moments have effective hooks.
Allowing any YouTube source video leaves the complete, educational, and standalone-moment criteria unchanged.
The initial trial was a distinct earlier task whose source-content rule is historical and is not modified by this later instruction.
Source-video flexibility does not change the background-music requirement or its mixing and selection rules.
The choice of source video does not change client approval authority, publication eligibility, or rejected-clip handling.
The extended trial was an earlier completed task, and the later source-selection permission does not revise its historical deliverable state.
The permission to choose any YouTube video does not change the 45-to-60-second duration rule.
The source decision does not alter the clean editing style or restrictions on distracting effects.
Choosing any YouTube source video does not remove or modify the requirement to integrate B-roll naturally where it supports the message.
The batch remains a five-clip live-publication deliverable; source-video selection is independently represented by the source Requirement.
Source-video flexibility does not change the white-text, brand-font, or no-effects caption rules.
